description:
For one day only, the charity Refugees at Home is holding a special photography exhibition at their home, International House. 

'Home Between Homes: The Faces Behind Hosting' showcases the stories of ordinary people who have opened their own homes to refugees.

events.name: Drop in: Home Between Homes: The Faces Behind Hosting
events.notes: Drop in for our photography exhibition showcasing the stories of ordinary people who have opened their own homes to refugees.

events.name: Hear from Refugees at Home and International House
events.notes: Join us from 6pm to hear from Refugees at Home and International House. Meet some of our hosts and hear about their experiences of hosting.

facilities: Handrails on both sides of stairs

factsheet.heading: The unique history of International House
paragraphs: International House is currently in the middle of an ongoing development battle that encompasses the current reality of this city.

The 12-storey building was previously used as an office by its owners, Lambeth Council, who vacated the premises in 2018 to save money. Since then, it has been an affordable working space for more than 100 organisations. Earlier this year, the council approved redevelopment plans to provide 288 new homes, 40% of which will be affordable housing.

factsheet.heading: A home for Refugees at Home
paragraphs: International House provides an affordable home to over 100 charities and community-focused organisations, including Refugees at Home.
The stability and sense of home that International House offers is vital for us as a charity that supports refugees who are facing street homelessness.

factsheet.heading: Home Between Homes: The Faces behind Hosting
paragraphs: The photography project - Home Between Homes: The Faces Behind Hosting - is a series of portraits created by photographer Eve Milner, who has been working with Refugees at Home pro bono, celebrating the people who have opened their homes to refugees and highlighting human connection at the centre. It spotlights 18 of our volunteer hosts from a range of backgrounds – from Herbert & Eva, a couple who fled World War 2, to footballer and broadcaster Gary Lineker. All portraits are taken inside hosts’ homes and showcase the welcoming environments created for their guests. The exhibition also features the stories of hosts involved, providing more insight on their experiences and motivations in making the UK a more welcoming place for people seeking sanctuary.

name: Refugees at Home at International House
